# Code review of apps/metis: merged report (09/10/2026)

Six pdev reviewer agents, run by hand (not through plan-audit), reading the code only. The controller merged 73 raw findings
by defect pattern and re-checked the heavy items with probes on a scratch copy of the code (the repo was not touched).
Task brief: `brief.md`. Raw findings of each agent: `audits/`. Probe evidence: `evidences/probes.md`.

## Conclusion

1. The two things the product owner noticed are right, and bigger than they look. Vietnamese text appears on 2.220 lines in 288 files;
   only 137 lines (the two `strings/vi.ts` dictionaries) are legitimate, and the rest are comments, test titles, messages
   of ESLint and the results of the gates. The values of the mock data (names, identifiers) are retyped on about
   339 lines in 53 test files; UI text is retyped on up to 495 lines in 58 test files, right next to the dictionary
   that already exists.
2. One mechanism produces both. The code was copied verbatim from the code blocks of the Vietnamese plans. The mock data module
   exports no identifier constants, so every place that uses them retypes them, the mock server included. The repo has no
   convention document for people who write code (the rules live only in CLAUDE.md, which git ignores). No gate blocks
   Vietnamese or retyped text, and the ESLint rule banning hard-coded text applies only to the design system.
3. The test suite reaches 100% coverage and 100% mutation testing but has blind spots, proven by probes: three defects that read
   the wrong metric field on screen 24 slip through all 704 related tests; the trace gate reports every id traced when the only
   test of a requirement id is marked `skip`; ESLint lets `src/core` import `expo-router`, lets `model.ts` import a
   React component, lets the shell write hard-coded text in JSX.
4. CI (the automated check system on GitHub) cannot be green yet: two jobs are cut off at 30 minutes, mutation testing needs
   75 minutes. The machine-written table in `apps/metis/reports/verify.md` still shows mutation testing RED; the green exists only in
   the hand-written passage after a rerun on one file alone.
5. There are real defects in the UI: from another workspace, clicking My focus makes the shell jump to Creative Studio; when
   loading the shell fails there is no retry button and the app user is told to "reload the page"; the Vietnamese version has two buttons with the same
   text "Viec cua toi" that lead to two different places; two places where text on Android skips the font selector; the search box promises the keyboard
   shortcuts ⌘K and "/" that do not exist.
6. Recommendation: one cleanup wave before plan C builds more screens, because every pattern here will be copied to about 50 screens.
   Order in the section "Recommended fix order".

## Needs a decision from the product owner

1. **Language convention of the code.** Context: a team of about 40 people at the agency will read the code; all six agents recommend the
   same. Recommendation: English for code, comments, test titles and tool messages; Vietnamese only in
   `strings/vi.ts` and the name of the language "Tieng Viet"; a comment gives the reason in one line, and does not point to plan decision
   ids (R-B15, D-B23) or wireframe line numbers; an automatic gate blocks it.
2. **Drop decision D-B23** (a page outside a workspace builds the shell with the HOME workspace). Context: while in Digital
   Products, clicking My focus changes the sidebar, the project tree and the "+ New" button to Creative Studio; plan B records
   the cost of D-B23 as "none". Recommendation: remember the workspace just viewed, use HOME only when the app is first opened.
3. **Vietnamese text for the "My items" scope button on screen 24.** Context: it and the sidebar entry "My focus" are both
   "Viec cua toi"; the button "Ve Viec cua toi" reads like "back to my item". Recommendation: keep "Viec cua toi" for My
   focus, change "My items" to "Hang muc cua toi" (proposed text, awaiting approval).
4. **Mutation testing in CI.** Context: spec 11.1 already set mutation testing on the changed code of each pull request
   and a full run on a schedule; `gate:mutation` has only the full run. Recommendation: follow spec 11.1 exactly
   (`stryker run --incremental` for each pull request; the full run on a schedule, with a time limit above the measured time).
5. **Commit first, clean up after.** Context: the repo has no commit yet; the cleanup will touch about 300 files. Recommendation:
   commit the current state (plans A, B, narrow widths) first, so that the cleanup becomes a readable diff.

## Recommended fix order

1. **Convention and language gate.** `apps/metis/CONTRIBUTING.md`, one page in English. One ESLint rule that scans comments
   and strings and reports non-ASCII text outside an allow list (not only the class of Vietnamese diacritics: that class
   misses "dung", "mau", "va" on 28 lines). Add a reverse test (plant a defect to prove the gate catches it) for the new rule.
   Translate the ESLint messages and the gate results first (that is the interface of the gates), then comments and
   test titles. Keep requirement ids (OVW-01, BR-24, D-19) at the start of test titles, because the trace gate reads them. Fix
   at the same time the reverse test that pins the string "spec 5.5" in a Vietnamese message (`scripts/canary.mjs:135`)
   and the 22 lines of script tests that assert the exact Vietnamese sentence printed.
2. **One source for mock data and text.** `src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts` for workspace ids, project ids and names; the mock
   server, config, e2e (one `e2e/web/paths.ts`) and the release check script read from there. Tests take their values
   from the mock data and `STRINGS`; each screen keeps only one test (`model.test.ts`) with hand-typed text as the reference. One
   ESLint rule for test files reports strings equal to a value of a dictionary or of the mock data. Extend the rule on text in
   JSX to the shell, screens and routes.
3. **Shared test harness.** One place for the fake clock, the mock server, mock storage, mounting a screen with the real
   route; one mock data variant per screen with "all numbers different"; the three assertions still missing on screen 24.
4. **Gates.** The trace gate ignores `skip`, `todo`, `fixme` and counts ids per screen; one shared Playwright
   fixture fails a test when a request escapes the mock server; `forbidOnly: true` and record the number of tests in the
   report; `verify.md` records the stamp of the code tree; CI splits mutation testing per spec 11.1.
5. **Architecture for plan C.** Move the shared parts of the screens (the data-fetching hook, mapping errors to states,
   StateView, the state text) out of screen 24; separate the project header from the contract of the overview screen; patch
   the loopholes in the boundary rule and add reverse tests for the two rows that do not have them yet.
6. **UI defects** in the Major group (shell, Vietnamese, Android) then the Nits.

## What is good (the agents checked and found clean)

`src/core/api/client.ts` never throws, every failure becomes a typed `ApiError`; `useShell` and
`useOverview` discard a reply that arrives late; `isRouteId` blocks an empty id, `.` and `..` before any request; the 22 screen numbers of
`SCREENS` match `wireframes/manifest.json`; tokens have one source (`brand/tokens.css`, `gen-tokens.mjs`,
`gate:tokens`, e2e reads `tokens.css` at run time); shipped components take every label from a dictionary or a model;
`model.ts` is pure TypeScript; `contract.yaml` drives e2e and the trace gate; `serve-web.mjs` rejects paths that
escape the folder; the tests of the scripts are strong; there is no empty assertion yet in the tests of the shell.

## Findings, after merging

Level: 🔴 blocker = a real defect, or a gate or test that passes when the thing it guards is broken, or a pattern every new screen will copy
and that is costly to undo; 🟡 major = should be fixed before plan C; 💭 nit. "Checked" records how the controller checked the item itself;
an item without it is the agent's word, not re-checked. "Details" names only the file in `audits/` and the key of the raw finding.

### 🔴 1. Code, comments, test titles and tool messages are written in Vietnamese; no convention, no gate

- Seen by: all six agents.
- Measurement: 2.220 lines with Vietnamese text in 288 files (measured by the controller). Split by kind (architecture-reviewer,
  which also scanned json, yaml, html and so got 2.258): comments in shipped code, config and scripts 808 lines in
  170 files; comments in tests 556 lines in 100 files; test titles 489 lines in 105 files; messages
  of ESLint, of tools and of errors 75 lines in 17 files; test data 190 lines in 45 files (partly
  legitimate: testing the Vietnamese version); the two Vietnamese dictionaries 137 lines (legitimate).
- Comments pointing to plan decision ids or spec section numbers: 222 lines in 135 files; plus 78 lines pointing to wireframe line numbers
  (`wireframe.css:199`) and 7 lines of dated measurement log, in the design system and screen 24 alone.
  Those ids can only be resolved in 1,4 MB of Vietnamese plans.
- Checked: the messages of ESLint and of the trace gate are printed in Vietnamese in the probes (`evidences/probes.md`).
- Mechanism: agents copied the code blocks of the plan whole (the comment at `src/core/api/client.ts:6` is identical in two
  plan files); `apps/metis` has no README or CONTRIBUTING; no rule checks language.
- Consequence: when a gate is red, the message is the only guidance of the fixer, and it is now a Vietnamese sentence pointing to the Vietnamese spec
  (`eslint.config.js:119`; `verify.md` says "RED"). The important reasons sit in Vietnamese comments,
  for example why the language select on Android has opacity 0.01 (`src/design-system/Select.styles.ts:43-48`):
  someone who cannot read it will "clean up" and bring the old defect back. Every file that plan C writes will copy this style.
- Fix: step 1 of the fix order.
- Details: every file in `audits/`; keys `apps/metis#code-language-and-ruling-ids`, `tooling#language-of-code`,
  `src#ruling-id-comments`, `src/design-system+src/screens#vietnamese-comments`,
  `src/design-system+src/screens#reference-comments`, `src/shell#vietnamese-test-language`,
  `...tests#vietnamese-titles-comments`, `apps/metis/e2e+scripts#vietnamese-in-tests-and-tools`.

### 🔴 2. Mock data values and UI text retyped by hand throughout tests, e2e, the mock server, config and scripts

- Seen by: architecture-reviewer, code-reviewer part A, testability-reviewer parts A, B and C.
- Measurement (architecture-reviewer, exact match on string values): values of `src/mocks/fixtures/*.ts` retyped on 339
  lines in 53 test files; eight values ('creative-studio' 55, 'meridian-cgi-campaign' 49, 'Creative Studio' 18,
  'Nadia R.' 15, ...) account for 175 occurrences; 158 lines hand-type route paths; the overview path of Meridian is redefined
  in 8 e2e specs. The text of `strings/en.ts` is retyped on up to 495 lines in 58 test files (upper bound), while
  24 other test files already read from `STRINGS`: two parallel styles. On screen 24 alone (testability-reviewer part B):
  64 of 68 static sentences of `strings/en.ts` are retyped 194 times in 13 files.
- In shipped code: `src/mocks/handlers.ts:11-22` retypes the workspace id, the project id and the API address instead of reading
  them from the mock data and `apiConfig`; `src/platform/config.ts:8` (HOME) puts an id of the mock data into the release build;
  `scripts/check-web-release.mjs:14-17` keeps its own copy of four strings of the mock data.
- Checked: the number of occurrences of "Northwind Furniture Co" (19 lines, 13 files) and "Client Delivery" (9 lines, 6 files); read directly
  `handlers.ts`, `config.ts`, `src/platform/mocks.web.ts:13-14`.
- Mechanism: the mock data modules export only whole objects (the project id exists only at
  `creativeStudio.tree[0].programs[0].projects[0].id`); the code blocks of plan B come with the text already in them
  (`const MERIDIAN = [` at line 13121 of the plan); no shared test harness, no rule.
- Consequences heavier than the effort of the fix:
  - 7 "not shown" tests (asserting that a text does not appear) use hand-typed text as the key. After renaming in the mock
    data and fixing the red tests, those 7 tests will keep passing even if the defect returns, because nothing can draw a
    name that no longer exists (for example `src/shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:152`, `:164`).
  - Renaming the client "Northwind Furniture Co." leaves 4 of the 7 markers of the release check script matching
    nothing, yet the test of the script stays green because it uses its own copied strings.
  - The route table of `e2e/web/routes.spec.ts:9-32` copies by hand 21 of the 22 keys of `ROUTES`: a new destination of plan C
    will have no test that opens the path directly.
  - Point `apiConfig.baseUrl` at a real server and `handlers.ts:11` still matches only `https://api.metis.test`, and
    every request goes out to the real network without a warning (`onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass'`).
- Fix: step 2 of the fix order.
- Details: `round1-architecture-reviewer.md` (`src/mocks/fixtures#restated-fixture-ids`,
  `src/**/strings#copy-restated-in-tests`); `round1-code-reviewer-core-shell.md` (`src/mocks#fixture-ids-restated`);
  `round1-testability-reviewer-core-shell.md` (`src/mocks/fixtures#retyped-fixture-values`,
  `src/shell/strings#retyped-copy-in-tests`); `round1-testability-reviewer-design-screens.md`
  (`...#restated-copy-and-fixture`); `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`e2e/web#restated-literals`,
  `scripts/check-web-release.mjs#markers-restated`).

### 🔴 3. The trace gate can pass when no test of the requirement id runs

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C (blocker), code-reviewer part A (major).
- Checked by probe: changing the only test that carries the id BR-24 into `test.skip`, `scripts/check-trace.mjs` still
  prints "every id has a test carrying its name" and exits 0; the control (removing the id from the name) exits 1.
- Also (testability-reviewer part C, calling the function of the script directly): `test.todo`, `test.fixme` and an empty `describe` also
  count; the test titles of all screens are merged into one list, so a new screen that declares a shared id such as D-19 or
  BR-32 will be "traced" by the tests of screen 24. The test of the script (`check-trace.test.mjs:13-15`)
  asserts that `test.skip` is valid.
- Fix: ignore call chains with `skip`, `todo`, `fixme`; count only the names in the folder of that screen; add two cases
  to the test of the script and one reverse test.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`scripts/check-trace.mjs#vacuous-trace`);
  `round1-code-reviewer-core-shell.md` (`scripts/check-trace.mjs#skip-todo-count`).

### 🔴 4. CI cannot be green: two jobs are cut off at 30 minutes, mutation testing needs 75 minutes

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C.
- Checked (read directly): `.github/workflows/check.yml:27` and `:52` set `timeout-minutes: 30`; `reports/verify.md`
  measures `gate:mutation` at 4.527 seconds on a 10-core Mac; the reverse test of mutation testing runs it twice.
  The workflow has never run because the repo is not on GitHub yet.
- Consequence: from the first push, every pull request is red because it runs over the time limit.
- Fix: follow spec 11.1 exactly (decision item number 4); the reverse test of mutation testing mutates only the file with the planted defect.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`.github/workflows/check.yml#timeout-below-mutation`).

### 🟡 5. Three defects that read the wrong metric field on screen 24 slip through the whole test suite

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part B.
- Checked by probe: 3 of 3 planted defects all slipped through, and the 704 tests still passed. The Delayed tile is colored red according to the change
  against baseline; the Delayed tile shows the change instead of the number of delayed items; the risk card counts by the high-risk metric
  instead of the total of the list.
- Cause: Meridian has a delayed count of 2 equal to the change of 2, and a high-risk metric of 4 equal to the total of the risk list of 4;
  Showroom has 0 for both; the variants that already separate the two numbers assert a different field. 100% mutation testing
  cannot see it because Stryker has no mutator type that swaps field names.
- Fix: three assertions (`model.states.test.ts:173`, after `:236`, `ListCards.test.native.tsx:237-254`); a convention that each
  screen has a mock data variant with "all numbers different", with assertions on the whole model.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-design-screens.md` (`...model.states.test.ts#delayed-and-risk-field-swap`).

### 🟡 6. A request that escapes the mock server is not seen by 60 of the 75 browser tests

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C rated it blocker; the controller lowered it to major because it has not been proven that any
  test passed wrongly because of it.
- Checked (read directly): the mock server on the web runs `onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass', quiet: true`
  (`src/platform/mocks.web.ts:13-14`): a request with no handler goes out to the real network, with no log. The figure of 15 of the 75
  tests that turn on page error tracking is the agent's.
- Context: the trace-and-gaps plan records one escape (`ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` in `routes.spec`) and postponed the diagnosis.
- Fix: one Playwright fixture that turns itself on for every spec and fails the test when a request fails or a request to
  `api.metis.test` is not answered by the service worker; the e2e build reports an error instead of `bypass` for `api.metis.test`.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`e2e/web/support.ts#no-request-guard`).

- Shell: 125 `toHaveStyle` assertions, for example `TopBar.test.native.tsx:53-61` copies `TopBar.styles.ts:8-16` key
  by key; constant tables copied again (`src/core/routes.test.ts:3-52` copies `ROUTES` and `SCREENS`). Screen 24: 119
  `toHaveStyle` and 89 lines that walk the element tree (`.parent`, `.children`), mostly re-asserting the internal
  styles of the design system.
- Consequence: this kind of test agrees with a wrong value by construction (both copied from the same plan block); a single
  change to Banner in the design system turns red the tests of every screen that has a Banner.
- Fix: a convention by layer (the design system proves the appearance; a screen proves its own content, links, roles and
  layout); replace the constant tables with a property that can fail (every number of `SCREENS` appears in
  `wireframes/manifest.json`); use `testID` instead of walking the tree.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-core-shell.md` (`src/shell#mirror-tests`);
  `round1-testability-reviewer-design-screens.md` (`...blocks/*.test.native.tsx#ds-internals-in-screen-tests`).

### 🟡 18. The report `verify.md` is not bound to the code tree that was checked and does not record the number of tests

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C. Checked (read directly): the table written by the machine says `gate:mutation | RED`; the green is in
  the hand-written passage; the line "Commit: no commit yet", no stamp of the code tree. The task brief of the controller itself
  misread this report (it says 2.639 tests and 108 browser tests; the report says 2.663 and 160).
- Fix: `verify.mjs` records the hash stamp of the code tree and the number of tests of each gate; add `--only <gate>` that records the rerun row
  by machine instead of a paragraph.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`scripts/verify.mjs#report-not-bound-to-tree`).

### 🟡 19. Nothing fails when browser tests stop running

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C. Checked (read directly): `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`
  (`playwright.config.ts:8`), so `pnpm verify` on the Mac accepts a `test.only`; `skip` passes everywhere; the number of browser
  tests changed 100, 108, 160 and no machine recorded it.
- Fix: `forbidOnly: true`; a JSON report and a floor on the number of tests; an ESLint rule banning `only`, `skip` in tests.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`apps/metis/playwright.config.ts#no-run-floor`).

### 🟡 20. The browser layout tests are negative tests with no control; `gate:web` has no reverse test

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C.
- Four functions (`clipped`, `overflowing`, `smallTargets`, `outsideFrames`) return the broken elements of a set that is never
  counted; the set of text selected by `[dir="auto"]` goes blind when a Text sets `lang`. The reverse tests of R-T12 and R-N34
  were a one-off manual edit, not repeatable.
- Fix: return `{ checked, bad }` and assert `checked` above a floor; one self-check per function; a reverse test
  that plants a 30 px tap target.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts#negative-oracles-unproven`).

### 🟡 21. The gate "text laid out like iOS and Android" is a CSS emulation; no gate runs the native flows required by spec 11.2

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C.
- The emulation is calibrated on the very defect it generates (R-N34), and does not simulate the second native difference on record
  (R-N28). Spec 11.2 puts the Maestro flows on the iOS Simulator inside `pnpm verify`; `package.json` has no native gate.
  `review.md` (line 357) already records that the flows generated from the contract are still missing; under rule FE-23 this gap comes first in the review package.
- Fix: add `gate:native` on the Mac, or rename the 32 tests to say what they actually measure and record native layout
  checking as an open item.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts#yoga-emulation-in-sample`).

### 🟡 22. The line that decides the exit code of `verify`, `canary`, `check-trace` is outside coverage and has no test

- Seen by: testability-reviewer part C.
- Consequence: deleting `process.exitCode = code` (`verify.mjs:67`) makes `pnpm verify` exit 0 even with a red row, and CI is green.
- Fix: a test that runs the real script in a temporary folder, following the pattern of `check-web-release.test.mjs:96-106`.
- Details: `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (`scripts/verify.mjs#cli-exit-unpinned`).

### 🟡 23. The `contract.yaml` of screen 24 describes only the desktop version

- Seen by: code-reviewer part B. Checked (read directly): 0 lines mention `legend`.
- On phones and in the native app, `status-*` is a View with no role and the drill-down link sits at `legend-*`,
  which the contract does not declare; the element type of the contract (`e2e/web/contract.ts:16-20`) has no width field.
- Fix: declare `legend-*` and record at which width each element is a link; run the "undeclared control" test at
  phone width.
- Details: `round1-code-reviewer-design-screens.md` (`...contract.yaml#phone-tier-undeclared`).

### 🟡 24. A drill-down value with a comma becomes two values after a round trip through the path

- Seen by: code-reviewer part A. Checked (read directly): `src/core/routes.ts:83` splits every value on commas;
  the contract accepts any non-empty string.
- Fix: forbid commas in the contract (one line of zod) and write that rule into the contract sent to the back end.
- Details: `round1-code-reviewer-core-shell.md` (`src/core/api/overview.ts#drill-comma`).

### 🟡 25. Avatar initials have two sources; the client-side rule gives collisions with Vietnamese names

- Seen by: code-reviewer part B.
- The shell receives `initials` from the server; screen 24 computes the first two initials itself (`model.lists.ts:12-18`): "Nguyen Thi Mai" and
  "Nguyen Thi Lan" both come out as "NT".
- Fix: add `initials` to the workload row of the contract as the contract of the shell does, or move the function into `src/core`.
- Details: `round1-code-reviewer-design-screens.md` (`...model.lists.ts#initials-source`).

### 🟡 26. Optional props of the design system do not accept `undefined`, so call sites must write the JSX twice

- Seen by: code-reviewer part B. Checked (read directly): `tsconfig.json:8` turns on `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.
- Example: `StateView.tsx:76-87` repeats the whole StatePanel element to add or drop `glyph`.
- Fix: declare `prop?: T | undefined` as `Legend.tsx:14` already does.
- Details: `round1-code-reviewer-design-screens.md` (`src/design-system#optional-props-undefined`).

## How the review was done

- Six pdev agents ran in parallel, each with one scope:

  | Agent | Scope | Findings file |
  |---|---|---|
  | `architecture-reviewer` | the whole app, design level; ran the skill `ponytail:ponytail-review` (a check for superfluous work) | `round1-architecture-reviewer.md` (11) |
  | `code-reviewer` part A | shipped code of core, platform, mocks, routes, shell, scripts, config | `round1-code-reviewer-core-shell.md` (15) |
  | `code-reviewer` part B | shipped code of the design system and screen 24 | `round1-code-reviewer-design-screens.md` (16) |
  | `testability-reviewer` part A | tests of core, platform, mocks, shell | `round1-testability-reviewer-core-shell.md` (9) |
  | `testability-reviewer` part B | tests of the design system and screen 24 | `round1-testability-reviewer-design-screens.md` (8) |
  | `testability-reviewer` part C | e2e, tests of the scripts, the gates | `round1-testability-reviewer-e2e-gates.md` (14) |

- The agents only read code and ran no Jest or any heavy tool, because at the time of assignment a Stryker run of another session
  was occupying 5 CPU cores.
- The controller: measured before assigning the work (the two strings the product owner named, Vietnamese text, decision ids in
  comments); after the findings came in, ran 3 wrong-field probes, 7 ESLint probes and 3 trace gate probes
  (each negative probe with a control), and read about 20 places directly (`evidences/probes.md`).
- Merge: 73 raw findings into 4 blockers, 22 majors, 28 nits. Two items changed level compared with the agent: requests that escape
  the mock server (blocker to major) and the "stale reply" test (major to nit), the reasons are recorded in each item.
